doc.title: Phil Wilson interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 27, 2023

title: Billy May's 'Sort of Dixie'
summary: Wilson praises Billy May's 'South Rampart Street Parade' arrangement and its sense of a parade passing.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Listening to classical music, then and now

blocks.x: Well we’ve been at this for about an hour. I’ve got a couple of more questions. This one, I don’t know if this is bad interviewing style but I know the answer to this but I’m going to ask you anyway.
Are you familiar with the Billy May recording “Sort of Dixie”?

Yes. I love it. Especially “South Rampart Street Parade.” That son of a bitch is an absolute genius. You know it’s the march [scats]. Right? And he’s — this is high fidelity. We’re not in stereo yet. Stereo did not exist when he recorded that. That is — the state of the art was high fidelity. You remember that. And he wrote that song so when you play it you can actually feel the parade going by you and continuing down the street. How did he pull that off?
That the musicians got through it without sort of cracking up sometimes. I mean it sounds like Spike Jones meets Sauter-Finegan or something.
